strategy.summary: Build NumPy from source at the buggy commit f15a116ee12e under Python 3.12, then run the new test test_unsigned_resize on the buggy revision (expected to fail) and on the fixed revision (expected to pass). The defect is in numpy.resize: repeats = -(-new_size // a.size) negates an unsigned new_size, which wraps and produces a huge repeats value, so the test errors (RuntimeWarning, then SystemError or OverflowError) before reaching its assertion. The fix uses (new_size + a.size - 1) // a.size.

pip_packages: numpy (built from source at the commit under test, not from PyPI)
system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang) and git
build_commands: git checkout f15a116ee12e && git submodule update --init
pinned_because: Python 3.12 is taken from the issue environment (site-packages path in traceback), not from a documented constraint.
numpy is not pinned to a version: the source tree itself is the system under test, so the version is whatever the buggy and fixed commits contain.
pytest and hypothesis are documented in README Testing section as required, but no version is pinned; the latest versions compatible with the build requirements are used.

strategy.reproducing_test: numpy/_core/tests/test_numeric.py::test_unsigned_resize (method of the resize test class, selected with -k test_unsigned_resize): for (np.int32, np.uint32) and (np.int64, np.uint64) pairs, asserts np.resize(arr, unsigned(1)) equals np.resize(arr, signed(1)) for arr = [[23, 95], [66, 37]].
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision f15a116ee12e the test fails: the first iteration's np.resize(arr, np.uint32(1)) emits RuntimeWarning 'overflow encountered in scalar negative' and then raises SystemError (or the 64-bit pair raises OverflowError), so the test errors before its equality check. On the fixed revision (the commit with repeats = (new_size + a.size - 1) // a.size) both pairs return [23] for signed and unsigned sizes, assert_array_equal passes, and the test passes.
strategy.numerical_probe: np.resize(np.array([[23, 95], [66, 37]]), np.uint32(1)) should return array([23]) with no warning on the fixed revision.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: RuntimeWarning: overflow encountered in scalar negative; SystemError: <built-in function concatenate> returned NULL without setting an exception
OverflowError: cannot fit 'numpy.uint64' into an index-sized integer

risks: The failure mode depends on platform and allocator: the issue reports SystemError for uint32 and OverflowError for uint64; another platform may instead raise MemoryError or hang while allocating a huge repeats array. Any of these still counts as a failure on the buggy revision, but the exact exception text will differ.
NumPy's pytest configuration may turn RuntimeWarning into an error via filterwarnings; if so the buggy run fails at the warning, which is still a transition but at a different line.

The reproduction only triggers on builds where unsigned scalar negation wraps (standard two's complement, which holds on all mainstream platforms); it cannot be expected to transition under a sanitiser or on an architecture where the resize path differs, and no such configuration is evidenced here.
The provided test_command (numpy.test()) is not the project's own test selector and would run the full suite; the pytest -k invocation is used instead.
Building the buggy and fixed commits requires a working compiler toolchain and submodules; a missing build dependency would produce an error that is not the target failure.
numpy, pytest and hypothesis have no documented or era-derived version constraint; the strategy chooses current versions compatible with the commit's build requirements.
Expected-value check relies on the signed-int result as the reference; the test compares arrays exactly, so no numeric tolerance applies.

oracle.reference_source: np.resize with the signed integer scalar of the same width (np.int32 / np.int64), as stated by the developer test
oracle.why: Resize only copies and repeats integer elements, so exact equality is the correct comparison and no floating-point tolerance is needed.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On f15a116ee12e the first call np.resize(arr, np.uint32(1)) hits repeats = -(-new_size // a.size) with unsigned new_size, which wraps to a large positive value; the buggy run emits RuntimeWarning and then raises SystemError (or OverflowError for uint64), so the test ends with an error before the assert_array_equal line is reached.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision repeats = (new_size + a.size - 1) // a.size gives 1 for both signed and unsigned size 1; both outputs equal [23] and assert_array_equal passes for both dtype pairs.
